text:
incident-bot: Pager: high-severity: infer-apac1 pool: 4/12 nodes NotReady; kubelet restarted multiple times. Observed spike in 5xxs on /v1/generate and increased latency. Auto-rollback disabled. Paging on-call.

alice (oncall): I'm taking this. Can folks drop logs here and I'll triage.

ben (infra): Ongoing from my side: nodes infer-apac1-node-02/05/09 flagged NotReady around the same window. kernel logs show OOM kills for runtime process on node-05.

carmen (runtime): copying relevant pod logs:
```
runtime: allocation failed: requested 1536MB
panic: runtime error: out of memory
...\nkubectl describe pod infer-runtime-55f8 -n inference
Events:
  Warning  OOMKilled  2m (x3 over 5m)  kubelet  Container killed due to OOM
```

ben (infra): Also grabbed dmesg from node-05:
```
[ 12345.678901] Out of memory: Kill process 21233 (redwood-runtime) score 924 or sacrifice child
[ 12345.679012] Killed process 21233 (redwood-runtime) total-vm:1223456kB, anon-rss:1130000kB
```

carmen (runtime): NVidia/errors from the same timeframe on node-05:
```
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=21233 GPU has fallen off the bus.
nvidia-smi: failed to initialize NVML: Uninitialized
```

alice (oncall): Sounds like a GPU driver/oom combo causing kubelet restarts and node NotReady. Is this limited to node-05, or correlated on others? Any CrashLoopBackOff states?

dave (sre): glance at cluster state: 3 pods in CrashLoopBackOff, 2 OOMKilled, nodes 02/05/09 NotReady. There's elevated error rate for customers using hosted small/generate route; support reported a handful of customers with 503s.

eve (support): CS escalations: two customers on dedicated accounts reported degraded latency, one reported intermittent 500s. No data exfiltration, customers are blocked for some calls. We told them we're investigating and will route traffic.

ben (infra): immediate mitigation plan: cordon node-05 and node-09, taint with inference=evac:NoSchedule, drain non-critical pods, restart kubelet on node-05 to see if it recovers, and reroute inference traffic off infer-apac1 to infer-us-central and infer-eu-west while we assess.

carmen (runtime): On runtime side: enabling smaller-ram fallback for heavy callers, and temporarily enable model-quantized variants on fallback routing. Also toggling prefix caching off for impacted routes to avoid large KV growth while we investigate.

alice (oncall): Action list:
- ben: cordon/drain 05 and 09, restart kubelet and node driver.
- carmen: add route fallback to other pools + enable quantized fallback.
- dave: watch customer 5xx surface and coordinate with support.
- eve: notify customers about mitigation and ETA.

ben (infra): running commands now:
```
kubectl cordon infer-apac1-node-05
kubectl drain infer-apac1-node-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
systemctl restart kubelet
# checking driver module
journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200 | tail -n 50
```

ben (infra): journalctl shows repeated "GPU has fallen off the bus" messages then kernel OOMs. I'm holding node offline for now. cordoned 05/09/02.

dave (sre): Traffic steering in progress: adding temporary routing rule in the control plane to send 30% of inference requests to infer-us-central and 20% to infer-eu-west, keeping rest on other healthy apac nodes. Monitoring latency and error rates.

carmen (runtime): Pushed routing patch: fallback model set to quantized-medium for heavy routes. Also restarted the runtime pod on node-08 to reduce memory pressure; restart was clean.

eve (support): Messaging update: notified top impacted customers, provided temporary endpoint suggestions and ETA ~30-45m. Customers acknowledged and appreciate transparency.

alice (oncall): Any sign of a bad driver update or kernel drift? Ben, what changed on node-05?

ben (infra): Node-05 recently cycled to driver v525.60 last night as part of our gradual rollout. Only 2/12 nodes on apac have the new driver; both experiencing issues. Rolling back driver on those nodes now.

carmen (runtime): Correlation looks strong: driver v525.60 + high contiguous allocations under heavy batched traffic => Xid 31 then OOMs. Possible memory leak in runtime when GPU reports off-bus. Creating a debug ticket for runtime crash path.

alice (oncall): Good catch. Ben, proceed with rollback on remaining nodes with v525.60 and hold further driver rollouts.

ben (infra): Rolling back on node-05 and node-09 now. Will validate with `nvidia-smi` and `kubectl get nodes`.

ben (infra): Post-rollback: `nvidia-smi` ok on node-05, no more Xid 31. kubelet stayed stable after restart. Marking node-05 as schedulable and uncordoning.

carmen (runtime): Runtime pods warming back up, no new OOMs on those nodes in the last 8 minutes. Error rate on /v1/generate falling back to baseline.

dave (sre): Customer 5xxs dropped to normal. Rolling back traffic steering after validating 15m of stable metrics.

eve (support): Update sent: nodes recovered after driver rollback; full service restored for affected customers. Close the high-priority ticket if everything holds.

alice (oncall): Handoff note: I'm wrapping this incident. Ben will continue watching infra, Carmen will own the runtime follow-up, and we'll create a post-incident ticket to stop driver rollouts until compatibility testing expanded.

deploy-bot: Deployment reverted: driver-rollout v525.60 -> v470.* on nodes infer-apac1-node-05,infer-apac1-node-09.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: infer-apac1 kubelet flaps due to GPU driver Xid 31 + OOM cascade. Follow-up ticket INFR-3421 created for driver rollout gating, runtime OOM path investigation, and improved canary throttles.

alice (oncall): Closing thread. If we see reoccurrence open an instant page. :white_check_mark:
